title: A grey stone found apart from the vein
summary: A shepherd of the ninth hearth, hunting a ewe caught in bracken a few miles north of Dùn ìseal, finds a grey stone with a bright wound where her stick scraped the moss away and carries it down out of curiosity. It sits on a sill at Dùn ìseal a season, turned over by whoever passes, before anyone thinks to put fire to it.

title: Fearchar Airgeadach smelts the first bead
summary: Fearchar, a basket-carrier of the ninth hearth who has spent three winters tending the vein's fires, builds his own fire apart from the Hall on the spur where the stone was found and feeds it through a day and half a night. Old Tormod, dozing beside him, wakes to find a bead of soft bright metal in Fearchar's hand that answers to no fire the Hall has ever kept.

title: Muileann chiar named
summary: Within a month Fearchar has raised a proper furnace of clay and dry stone on the spur and is hammering beads into rings. The households of the ninth hearth call the place Muileann chiar, the dark mill, after the smoke that hangs over it of a still morning, unmindful of the older place of that name far to the east.

title: Muireach Liath rules the silver shows no blood
summary: Asked whether the new metal falls under the flame, Muireach Liath presses a ring's softest edge with his thumbnail, finds no colour beneath the break as a coal always shows, and rules that the Hall has no claim on a thing that shows no colour when it breaks. Fearchar is left free to dig on, and to keep or give what he digs.

title: The first ring set out for Goibhniu
summary: Fearchar takes up the custom of setting the first ring off every new furnace whole on a flat stone at the mouth of the workings, an offering to Goibhniu, before a second ring is begun. No furnace of his ever fails in its first season, which the smiths of Muileann chiar take as proof the god has taken the offerings kindly.

title: Two cousins of the eastern share claim the silver ground
summary: Grandsons of one grandfather through different daughters, whose households have shared an unremarkable boundary along a dry burn since their grandfather's day, each send word to Dùn ìseal within days of the other, swearing the spur of Fearchar's furnaces lies on his own side of the burn. The keepers of the slab find the seam outside their reach to judge and send the cousins back to settle it themselves.

title: Fearchar pays a ring to each cousin
summary: Weary of digging under a dispute he did not start, Fearchar offers a ring from the season's working to each of the two cousins, on condition that both let the digging go on undisturbed while their elders argue the boundary. Both take the ring, neither gladly, and the quarrel is settled within the year by a boundary stone the two households cut and raise together at the driest point of the burn.

title: The first ring traded at Ros fhionn
summary: A carrier of the ninth hearth strikes the first known trade of a ring against a whole boatload of salted fish and sealskin at the river quays of Ros fhionn. The measure holds for every later bargain on the quay, so that a boatman naming a price says simply "a ring's worth" and is understood without further reckoning.

title: Death of Ceallach mac Ghille-Bhrìde
summary: Ceallach, who has kept the coal of the First Flame in the high valleys since his father Gille-Brìde's death, dies in his sleep at the age of a hundred and forty, the last of Somhairle's line in whom the long years still showed. His household carries the coal down to the Hall's own flame; his children leave the high valleys within the year and settle among the lower hearths.

title: Three candidates passed over for the flame
summary: On Muireach Liath's death the nine hearths weigh three households' candidates at length: a steady grandson of the sixth hearth, a daughter of the third hearth whose grandmother helped choose Beathag Bhàn, and Muireach's own nephew of the ninth hearth. All three are passed over in favour of Muireach's daughter Gormshuil, chosen on the work alone.

title: Muireach's nephew goes to the furnaces
summary: Passed over for the flame on the strength of blood alone, Muireach Liath's nephew of the ninth hearth goes north within the year to take up work at one of Fearchar's furnaces at Muileann chiar, where he is said to prosper a good deal more than he might have as a Keeper chosen by kinship rather than by the households' own will.
